name: q-lint
description: q/kdb+ for VS Code: linting, Quick Fixes, navigation and help from the source, and connections to q processes to run code on.

q-lint.enable.markdownDescription: Run the q-lint language server. Off, it starts no server: no diagnostics, Quick Fixes, formatting, navigation or semantic colouring. The grammar's colouring, processes, queries, the Process Explorer, notebooks and the agent tool stay.

q-lint.serverPath.markdownDescription: Path to the `qlinter` binary; a leading `~` is your home directory. Left empty, the extension uses the server it was packaged with, and falls back to `qlinter` on `PATH` when it was packaged without one or that one will not run. Set, it always wins.

q-lint.serverArgs.markdownDescription: Extra command-line arguments for `qlinter --lsp`, after the ones the other settings produce - for example `["--isolated"]` or `["--extend-select", "QS001"]`. Flags given here keep their command-line meaning, so unlike `#q-lint.lint.select#` they can widen what the repository's configuration selects.

q-lint.profile.markdownDescription: Which rules to run. Set here, it overrides `profile` in a repository's `qlinter.toml`; left unset, the repository's configuration decides, and `style` applies where there is none. `style` reports what q refuses and what q runs but is almost certainly a mistake. `general` keeps only what q itself rejects; `styleq` adds the conventions of published q style guides; `uqf` adds one repository's house conventions on top of those.

q-lint.configFile.markdownDescription: A configuration file to use for every document instead of the nearest `.qlinter.toml`, `qlinter.toml` or `pyproject.toml` `[tool.qlinter]` (the server's `--config`). Relative to the first workspace folder; a leading `~` is your home directory. Empty: the nearest one governs each file, as on the command line and in CI.

q-lint.lint.select.markdownDescription: Show only these rules, among those the configuration already turns on. Rule codes or prefixes, as `qlinter --rules` lists them. It narrows and never widens: a rule the repository's configuration leaves off stays off. Empty: no narrowing.

q-lint.lint.ignore.markdownDescription: Hide these rules in the editor. Rule codes or prefixes, as `qlinter --rules` lists them. Applied after the configuration, so it can only hide; the repository's configuration, which CI reads, is unchanged.

enumDescriptions: Lint the buffer on every change.
Lint when the file is opened and saved. Quick Fixes match the last saved lint, so they appear again after a save.

q-lint.lint.severity.markdownDescription: The severity the editor shows, by rule code or prefix; the longest that names a rule decides. For example `{"QS": "hint", "QE": "error"}`. Display only: what is reported does not change.

q-lint.fixes.unsafe.markdownDescription: Offer the editor-only Quick Fixes too: those `qlinter --fix` applies only with `--unsafe-fixes`, because they can change what a working program does or guess at what was meant. Off, only the fixes `qlinter --fix` applies are offered.

q-lint.format.enable.markdownDescription: Offer **Format Document**, which applies the fixes `qlinter --fix` applies and nothing else. Off, q-lint does not register as a formatter.

q-lint.semanticTokens.enable.markdownDescription: Colour functions where they are called and parameters where they are read, on top of the grammar's colouring. Off, only the grammar colours.

q-lint.navigation.enable.markdownDescription: Offer the outline, workspace symbols, **Go to Definition**, **Find All References**, occurrence highlights, **Rename Symbol** for a local or a global across the workspace - all read from the source, never by running it. Off, q-lint announces none of them: turn it off when another q extension already navigates and both would answer.

q-lint.help.enable.markdownDescription: Show a hover and signature help: for a name the workspace defines, its parameters, the comment above its definition and its file; for a word of q itself, how it is written and what it gives. Read from the source and a built-in catalogue, never from a running q. Off, q-lint announces neither.

q-lint.completion.enable.markdownDescription: Complete names as you type: a lambda's parameters and locals, the names the workspace's `.q` files define, and q's own words. It knows no table's columns and nothing only a running process holds. Off by default, because an editor that is told a server completes stops offering the words already in the file.

q-lint.callHierarchy.enable.markdownDescription: Offer **Show Call Hierarchy** on a global function: the definitions and files that name it, and the workspace functions its own definition names. Read from the source, never by running it, so a name used as a value counts as a call and a call made through a string is not seen. Off, q-lint does not announce it.

q-lint.graph.enable.markdownDescription: Offer the **q Dependencies** view - the files the active q file depends on and those depending on it - and **q-lint: List Affected Tests**, the test files that reach a q file changed against git HEAD. Both are what `qlinter analyze graph` prints. Off, the server answers neither and the view is hidden.

q-lint.rename.enable.markdownDescription: Offer **Rename Symbol** (F2): a lambda's parameter or local within its lambda, and a global in every workspace file that names it, under the `\d` each is written in. Needs `q-lint.navigation.enable`. Off, q-lint does not announce renaming, and the rest of navigation stays.

q-lint.inlayHints.enable.markdownDescription: Show parameter names at the arguments of a bracketed call to a workspace function - `f[a: 1; b: 2]` drawn over `f[1;2]` - for a function whose definitions all declare the same signature. Read from the source, never from a running q. VS Code's own `editor.inlayHints.enabled` hides them too, or shows them only while a key is held. Off, q-lint announces none.

q-lint.codeLens.enable.markdownDescription: Show **Run** above each function a statement at column 0 defines, and **Run test** above one named `test_*`. Run sends the definition to the connected process - under the `\d` it is written in - as a query from the editor would be sent; Run test sends it and then calls it with no argument. Off, q-lint announces no lenses.

q-lint.documentLinks.enable.markdownDescription: Make the path of each load - `\l lib/x.q`, `system "l lib/x.q"` or a file symbol `` `:lib/x.q `` - a link: Ctrl/Cmd+click opens the file, found against the workspace folder and then the loading file's own directory and each one above it, as **Go to Definition** on the path finds it. Off, q-lint announces no links.

q-lint.generateQdoc.enable.markdownDescription: Offer **Generate qDoc for f** in the lightbulb and **Refactor...** menu inside a function a statement at column 0 defines: it writes a `/ @param` line for each parameter and a `/ @return` line directly above the definition, for the descriptions to be typed after. Not offered where the comment above already has an `@param` or `@return`. Off, q-lint offers no such action.

q-lint.workspaceIndex.enable.markdownDescription: Read every `.q` file in the workspace at startup, never running it, so a name another file defines is not reported as undefined and is coloured as a function. Off, only open files are indexed.

q-lint.workspaceIndex.exclude.markdownDescription: Globs, relative to the workspace folder, of files and directories the workspace index does not read - for example `["vendor/**", "**/generated/**"]`. An open file is still linted and indexed. Whatever the configuration's `exclude` skips - by default `.git`, `.venv`, `node_modules`, `__pycache__`, `build`, `dist` and `target` - is skipped too, as `qlinter .` skips it.

q-lint.trace.server.description: Log the traffic between VS Code and the server, for debugging the integration itself.

q-lint.output.consoleSize.markdownDescription: Height and width, in characters, a query's result is formatted to (`.Q.S` on the process). A larger result is cut there, by the process, before it is sent.

q-lint.output.autoClear.markdownDescription: Clear the **q-lint: query** output before each result.

q-lint.output.includeQuery.markdownDescription: Show the code that was run above its result.

q-lint.output.ignoreNullReturn.markdownDescription: Show nothing for a query whose value is `::`, such as an assignment ending in `;`.

enumDescriptions: Show every result in the **q-lint: query** output, as q formats it.
Show a table, dictionary or list in the **q-lint: result** panel as a table you can sort, filter and copy as CSV. Anything else goes to the output.
Show a table, dictionary or list in the **q-lint: result** panel as a chart of its numeric columns. Anything else goes to the output.
q-lint.query.mode.markdownDescription: Where a query's result is shown. **q-lint: Switch Query Mode** changes it.

q-lint.query.gridLimit.markdownDescription: The most rows of a result the process sends to the grid or chart. The panel says when a result was cut, and how many rows it had.

q-lint.query.gridDecimals.markdownDescription: Decimal places the grid shows a float or real to, and copies as CSV. `-1`: as the process writes it, to its `\P` precision.

enumDescriptions: Open the **q-lint: result** panel beside the editor.
Show the result in the **q Results** view in the bottom panel, beside the terminal and the output.
q-lint.query.resultsLocation.markdownDescription: Where a grid or chart result is shown: beside the editor, or in the **q Results** view in the bottom panel.

q-lint.query.resultHistory.markdownDescription: How many grid or chart results the result panel keeps as tabs. **q-lint: Show Result from History** picks one too.

q-lint.results.history.enable.markdownDescription: Keep the last `q-lint.query.resultHistory` results as tabs in the result panel, and offer **q-lint: Show Result from History**.

q-lint.results.diff.enable.markdownDescription: Offer **Compare** in the result panel, and **q-lint: Compare Result with Previous Run**: mark what changed since the previous run of the same query. Off, no previous result is kept.

q-lint.results.statistics.enable.markdownDescription: Offer the result panel's **Stats** view, and **q-lint: Show Column Statistics**: each column's count, nulls, distinct values, min, max and mean.

q-lint.results.heatmap.enable.markdownDescription: Offer the grid's **Heatmap** button, and **q-lint: Toggle Result Heatmap**. Off, no column is coloured, whatever `q-lint.query.gridHeatmap` says.

q-lint.results.tree.enable.markdownDescription: Offer the result panel's **Tree** view of a dictionary or a nested list, and **q-lint: Show Result as Tree**. Off, the process is not asked for the tree.

q-lint.results.export.enable.markdownDescription: Offer **Export as...** in the result panel, **q-lint: Export Results As...** and **q-lint: Copy Results As...**: the rows shown as Excel, Parquet, JSON, a Markdown table or a q expression that rebuilds the table. Export to CSV is always offered.

q-lint.results.paging.enable.markdownDescription: Page through a result cut at `q-lint.query.gridLimit`: the process keeps the whole result as `.qlint.held`, and the grid asks it for the next `gridLimit` rows as it scrolls to the end, up to 1,000,000 rows. Off by default, because it defines `.qlint.held` on the process and holds the result there until the next grid query while paging is on (`.qlint.held:()` frees it). Never on a process tagged `prod`, and never in unwrapped mode.

q-lint.results.pivot.enable.markdownDescription: Offer the result panel's **Pivot** view, and **q-lint: Show Result as Pivot**: rows by one column, columns by another, and the count, sum, average, min or max of a third.

q-lint.results.charts.enable.markdownDescription: Offer the area, step and candle charts, a second y axis, the chart's **Save PNG** and **Save SVG** buttons, and **q-lint: Save Result Chart as Image**. Off, the chart offers line, bar, scatter and histogram.

q-lint.results.drilldown.enable.markdownDescription: Offer the drill-down queries of `q-lint.results.drilldownTemplates` on a grid cell: double-click it, or right-click it and choose **Drill Down from Cell**. The query picked runs on the process the result came from, after a confirmation on a production one.

label.description: What the pick shows. The query, when there is no label.

query.description: The q to run. {{value}} is the cell's value as q, {{column}} its column's name as a symbol, {{row.name}} the value of column name in the same row.

columns.description: The columns it is offered for. Every column when left out.

q-lint.results.drilldownTemplates.markdownDescription: Follow-up queries a grid cell offers. In `query`, `{{value}}` is the cell's value as a q literal (`` `AAPL ``, `2024.01.02`, `0Nj`), `{{column}}` its column's name as a symbol, and `{{row.name}}` the value of column `name` in the same row. For example `{"label": "Trades", "query": "select from trade where date={{row.date}}, sym={{value}}", "columns": ["sym"]}`.

q-lint.query.gridHeatmap.markdownDescription: Colour the grid's numeric columns by value, in the theme's chart colours: blue from the least to the greatest, or, for a column either side of zero, blue above it and red below. **q-lint: Toggle Result Heatmap** and the grid's **Heatmap** button change it.

q-lint.query.unwrapped.markdownDescription: Send a query as a plain string, statement by statement, for a gateway that refuses a lambda, instead of in the lambda q-lint runs it with. The result is whatever the process returns, formatted by q-lint rather than the process, so it is close to q's console but not exact, and an error has no backtrace. **q-lint: Toggle Unwrapped Query** changes it.

q-lint.query.timeout.markdownDescription: Seconds a query may run before it is aborted, as **q-lint: Abort Current Query** aborts it; the history records it as timed out. `0`: no limit.

q-lint.query.progress.enable.markdownDescription: Count a running query's time in the status bar, and notify the end of one that ran `#q-lint.query.notifyAfter#` seconds while the window was not focused. Off: the status bar only spins, and nothing is notified.

q-lint.query.notifyAfter.markdownDescription: Seconds a query must run for VS Code to notify you when it ends while its window is not focused, with `#q-lint.query.progress.enable#` on. `0`: never notify.

q-lint.query.placeholders.enable.markdownDescription: Ask for a value for each `{{name}}` in the code a query sends, outside strings and comments, and put it in place before the query runs. Each box starts from the value given last. `{{x}}`, `{{y}}` and `{{z}}` are q lambdas and never asked for; turn this off if your code holds others, such as `{{a}}`.

q-lint.processExplorer.excludedNamespace.markdownDescription: Namespaces the **Process Explorer** and live completion leave out, without the leading dot: a root namespace (`q`) or a nested one (`ns.sub`). The namespaces nested in them are left out with them.

q-lint.processExplorer.previewLimit.markdownDescription: Rows of a table **Preview** shows in the **q-lint: query** output.

q-lint.processExplorer.autoRefresh.markdownDescription: Read the active process again after each query, so the **Process Explorer** and live completion show what it defined. Off, they are read on connect and on **Refresh Process Explorer**.

q-lint.queryHistory.search.enable.markdownDescription: **Filter Query History** and **Export Query History**. Off: their buttons and commands are hidden, and a filter set is cleared.

q-lint.processMonitor.refreshInterval.markdownDescription: Seconds between reads of the connected process while the **Process Monitor** is shown. `0`: read on connect and on **Refresh Process Monitor** only. A read never interrupts a query: it waits, or skips its turn.

q-lint.processExplorer.functionSource.en.markdownDescription: **Open Function Source**, **Edit and Redefine** and **Redefine on Process**. Off, their commands are hidden and send nothing.

q-lint.processExplorer.findCallers.enabl.markdownDescription: **Find Callers in Process**. Off, its command is hidden and sends nothing.

q-lint.processExplorer.tableHover.enable.markdownDescription: A table row's tooltip in the **Process Explorer** asks the process for the table's `meta`, rows and memory when first shown. Off, it shows what the explorer already read.

q-lint.processExplorer.editorTableHover..markdownDescription: A hover on a table's name in a q editor asks the connected process for its `meta`, rows and memory. Off by default: it queries the process whenever the mouse rests on a table's name.

q-lint.processMonitor.enable.markdownDescription: The **Process Monitor** view. Off, it is hidden and reads nothing.

q-lint.hdbBrowser.enable.markdownDescription: The **HDB Browser** view. Off, it is hidden and reads nothing.

q-lint.query.tagQuery.enable.markdownDescription: **Query a Tag**: run one query on every saved and discovered process carrying a tag, each over a connection of its own, and show the answers as one table with a `process` column first; a process that fails is a row with its error.

q-lint.query.compare.enable.markdownDescription: **Compare Query Across Two Processes**: run one query on two processes, each over a connection of its own, and show the answers side by side with the cells that differ marked.

q-lint.savedQueries.enable.markdownDescription: The **Saved Queries** view: named queries kept for the workspace, run on the active connection, edited as q documents of their own, renamed and deleted. Off, the view is removed and its commands refuse; the queries are kept.

q-lint.query.watch.enable.markdownDescription: **Watch Query**: run a query on the active connection every few seconds and refresh its result in place until stopped, disconnected, or connected elsewhere. Off by default, as it sends code on its own; off, the command is hidden and refuses, and a watch running stops.

q-lint.query.watch.interval.markdownDescription: Seconds between a watched query's runs that **Watch Query** offers, with `#q-lint.query.watch.enable#` on.

q-lint.terminal.qBinary.markdownDescription: The q binary **Run Code from Terminal**, **Start q REPL** and **Send ... to Terminal** start: a name on `PATH` or a path, where a leading `~` is your home directory. It is quoted for the terminal's shell, so it is one program, not a command line with arguments. Read for the file's workspace folder.

q-lint.terminal.envPath.markdownDescription: A file of `NAME=value` lines set for q in a q terminal (**Run Code from Terminal**, **Start q REPL**, **Send ... to Terminal**), such as `QHOME` and `QLIC`, on the command line that starts it, so they win over the shell's startup files. Relative to the workspace folder, which may set its own; a leading `~` is your home directory. Values are taken as written: `$HOME` is not expanded.

q-lint.discovery.refreshInterval.markdownDescription: Minutes between fetches of every discovery server's process list, at most 1440. `0` fetches only on **Reload Discovery Server**, and when a server is added or edited.

q-lint.notebook.rowLimit.markdownDescription: The most rows of a table a notebook's `@grid` or `@chart` cell is sent; the process cuts it. `0`: every row. **q-lint: Set Notebook Row Limit** changes it.

enumDescriptions: Show a larger table's first rows.
Show a larger table's last rows, such as the latest of a table in time order.
q-lint.notebook.rowLimitFrom.markdownDescription: Which rows of a table larger than `#q-lint.notebook.rowLimit#` a notebook cell shows: its first or its last.

q-lint.notebook.variables.enable.markdownDescription: Show the **Notebook Variables** view: the globals on the process a q notebook's cells ran on, read with one lambda that defines nothing, only after a cell runs or on Refresh, and only while the view is open. Off, the view is removed and nothing is read.

q-lint.notebook.parameters.enable.markdownDescription: Turn on **q-lint: Run Notebook with Parameters** and the `/ @parameters` cell directive. Off, the command is hidden and refuses, and a cell with `/ @parameters` is not run. The shell's `node out/qnbrun.js` does not read VS Code's settings.

q-lint.notebook.export.enable.markdownDescription: Turn on **Export Notebook as HTML**, **Export Notebook as Jupyter Notebook** and **Import Jupyter Notebook as q Notebook**. Off, they are hidden and refuse. Export Notebook as q Script is not affected.

q-lint.notebook.liveValues.enable.markdownDescription: Read the `{{q: expr}}` live values of a q notebook's Markdown cells on the process. They are read only when you run the code cell above them, never on their own. Off, no expression is sent; values a run kept before still show.

q-lint.notebook.processDirective.enable.markdownDescription: Honour the `/ @process <label>` cell directive, which connects to that process before the cell runs (a production process is confirmed first). Off, a cell with it is not run, and nothing is sent.

q-lint.agent.queryTimeout.markdownDescription: Seconds a query run by an agent through the **Run q Query** tool may take. A query that takes longer is aborted, as **Abort Current Query** aborts one, and the agent is told it timed out. `0` sets no limit.

additionalProperties.patternErrorMessage: A theme colour id, such as charts.purple.

q-lint.processes.tagColors.markdownDescription: The colour of each tag in the Processes view, as a theme colour id: `{"eu": "charts.purple"}`. Over the built-in colours (`prod` red, `uat` blue, `dev` green); a process takes its most cautious tag's colour. **Edit Tag Color** on a tag row writes it.

q-lint.processes.readOnlyGuard.enable.markdownDescription: Before code is sent to a process carrying a tag `#q-lint.processes.readOnlyGuard.tags#` names, read it, and when it would assign a global, delete or update a table in place, write a file or run a system command, ask first. It holds for queries, Query a Tag, Compare Query, saved and watched queries, notebook cells, Redefine on Process and connect scripts; an agent's query that would change such a process is refused. It reads the code's text, so it is a check against a slip, not a permission system.

q-lint.processes.readOnlyGuard.tags.markdownDescription: The tags whose processes `#q-lint.processes.readOnlyGuard.enable#` guards, ignoring case. An empty list guards none.

q-lint.connection.connectScript.enable.markdownDescription: Run a process's connect script (**Set Connect Script**) on every connect. Off: no script runs, and **Set Connect Script** is hidden; the scripts stay in the process list.

q-lint.connection.heartbeat.enable.markdownDescription: Send a heartbeat on the active connection every `#q-lint.connection.heartbeatInterval#` seconds: a `::` sent as a plain string, whose round trip the status bar shows (`q: rdb 3 ms`). One the process has not answered for 5 seconds shows as `no answer`. It is skipped while a query runs. Off by default: a process that logs its clients sees every heartbeat.

q-lint.connection.autoReconnect.enable.markdownDescription: Reconnect when the process or the network drops the connection, waiting 1, 2, 4... seconds (at most 30) before each try, up to `#q-lint.connection.reconnectAttempts#` tries. The process's connect script runs again. **Disconnect**, or connecting to another process, stops it; a connection you closed is never reopened.

q-lint.connection.reconnectAttempts.markdownDescription: How many times `#q-lint.connection.autoReconnect.enable#` tries before it gives up.

q-lint connects only to a process you add here, and runs only the code you send it.

[Connect to Process](command:q-lint.connectProcess)
No queries yet. In a q file, Ctrl+Q runs the current line, Ctrl+R the selection and Ctrl+E the block on the connected process. Each query is kept here, with its outcome and time, to rerun.

[Get Started](command:q-lint.getStarted) with q-lint, or read the [documentation](https://github.com/kwojdalski/q-lint/blob/master/editors/vscode/README.md) and the [rule reference](https://github.com/kwojdalski/q-lint/blob/master/docs/rules.md).
Found a problem? [Report a bug](https://github.com/kwojdalski/q-lint/issues/new?labels=bug) or [suggest a feature](https://github.com/kwojdalski/q-lint/issues/new?labels=enhancement).

[Connect to Process](command:q-lint.connectProcess)

Not connected to a q process. Connect to an HDB to browse its partitions, the rows of each table in them, and its sym file.
[Connect to Process](command:q-lint.connectProcess)

languageModelTools.name: q-lint_runQuery
languageModelTools.userDescription: Run a q query on the active q process, or on one named by its label, and get the result as JSON.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Runs q (kdb+) code on a q process the user has set up in the q-lint extension, and returns the result as JSON. Without `process`, the code runs on the active connection, the process the user is connected to; with `process`, a label from the user's q-lint process list (a process listed by a discovery server is `server/label`), q-lint connects to that process first and it becomes the active connection. The code is run as the process's console runs a script: each line is a statement, indented lines continue the one above, and the value of the last statement is returned. Nothing is defined on the process except what the code itself defines, so prefer queries that only read. The user confirms every call, and a query that runs longer than the user's timeout (30 s unless set) is aborted. The result is one of three JSON objects. A table, keyed table, dictionary (as columns `key` and `value`) or list (as one column `value`) gives `{columns, types, rowCount, data, keyColumns?, columnCount?, truncated?}`: `columns` the column names, `types` their q types, `rowCount` how many rows the whole result has, `data` its first 200 rows as arrays of values, `keyColumns` how many leading columns are keys, `columnCount` how many columns it has when that is more than the 100 given, and `truncated: true` when `data` holds fewer rows than `rowCount` or fewer columns than `columnCount`. In `data`, booleans and numbers are JSON values and nulls are null; temporal values (timestamps, dates, times, timespans), symbols, guids and nested values are strings as q prints them, and so are longs beyond 2^53 and infinities (`0W`, `-0w`). Any other value - an atom, a string, a function - gives `{output}`, q's console text of it. A failure gives `{error, trace?}`: q's error and its backtrace (its first 40 lines), or why nothing ran - no process connected, an unknown label (the error lists the known labels), a timeout or a cancellation. Ask for only the rows and columns needed (`select ... where ...`, `n#t`), since at most 200 rows come back.

query.description: The q code to run. Several lines run in order, as a script; the last statement's value is returned.

process.description: The label of the q process to run on, as the user's q-lint process list names it (`server/label` for a discovered one). Omit to use the active connection.

[Add Process](command:q-lint.addProcess)
